- Dedicated asks: Reserved capacity with burst autoscale, predictable concurrency (peak concurrent generations ~45), and a warm KV cache for session-based tool calls.

1) Can you confirm expected concurrent generations and typical prompt sizes (avg tokens in/out)? Priya said she would surface this — we need it for the throughput model.

On Wed, Jul 14, 2026 at 09:12, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (post-call recap)

Thanks Rishi — adding technical notes and open questions from my side. High-level proposal follows; I'll put numbers into the modeling sheet after we get the token-size confirmation from Acme.

Notes / clarifications needed from Acme:
- Typical prompt length (tokens in) and response length (tokens out) for the customer-facing chat path. Do you stream tokens or buffer full responses?
- Embeddings/rerank: how many candidate embeddings per query, and nightly throughput window (wall-clock hours for batch)?
- Auth: you mentioned SAML SSO for users and a separate machine-to-machine key for batch jobs — confirm if the latter will run from Acme infra or via Redwood Private.

Initial Dedicated config (draft):
- Instance class: 4xA100 (or equivalent 80GB) nodes behind the Redwood serving runtime.
- Concurrency / queues: cap per node = 12 concurrent inflight generations (default soft), global concurrency target = 48; global queue depth = 120 (3x concurrency) with prioritized routing for interactive sessions.
- Autoscale: floor = 2 nodes, target scale-up at 65% CPU/GPU util sustained >90s, burst to +25% for short spikes; scale-down with 10m cooldown.
- KV cache: pin hot prefixes to keep session latency at p50; suggested TTLs for cache entries = 8h (configurable).
- Fallbacks: a smaller-but-fast quantized model variant for read-only tasks and a reranker-only pathway for embeddings hits to reduce cost.

Structured output/tool-calls: use the SDK's tool-calling primitives, prefer function-call mode with explicit schema to reduce sampling variance and cost; stream responses to the client when using long-running tool calls.

I will draft redwood-proposed-dedicated-config.yaml with these values and the throughput spreadsheet.

Thanks — helpful summary. Quick answers from our side:

- Average user prompt: 24 tokens in, 180 tokens out (mostly templated responses but some structured metadata). Peak interactive QPS we expect ~5–6 reqs/s (burst up to 9 reqs/s) during business hours. Nightly batch (reranker): ~1.2M queries over a 3-hour window; embeddings size per item ~1536 dims, candidates per query ~50.
- We stream to customers for interactive flows. Machine-to-machine batch jobs will originate from Acme batch cluster (on-prem) and use a dedicated machine API key; we prefer the Private control plane or VPC option for strict data separation.
- Auth: SAML for user-facing; M2M keys rotated via our vault.

Two asks for Redwood to confirm:
1) Queue sizing guidance for handling 9 reqs/s short bursts while keeping P95 token latency below 300ms.
2) A recommended autoscale policy that minimizes cold-start latency for the nightly reranker window (we prefer keeping a warm pool but want to avoid idle cost).

If you can provide a short note on those two items, we'll confirm budget and move to contract redlines next week.

—Arnold
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Financial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: Dedicated sizing proposal + autoscale pattern for Acme

Rishi / Ben — internal note before I send back to Acme with recommended config. Pulling Arnold's numbers into the model: 5–9 reqs/s burst, avg tokens 24/180, nightly rerank 1.2M over 3h.

Proposed adjustments (summary):
- Concurrency tuning: with response sizes ~180 tokens, effective token throughput = ~(requests/s * tokens_out). For interactive path target concurrency 48 is still reasonable; set per-node concurrency = 12 as Ben suggested. For 9 reqs/s bursts, a 4-node cluster (12 concurrency each) gives headroom with queue depth 72.
- Queue sizing: use two logical queues — interactive-priority (size=48) and batch-backfill (size=300). Prioritize interactive requests with preemption up to 30% of batch pool during business hours.
- Autoscale pattern: floor = 2 nodes (to keep KV cache warm), warm reserve = 1 extra node that can be pre-warmed via a scheduled policy 30m before expected rerank window. For reranker window, schedule a scale-to-target (4 nodes) 40 minutes before the start time; allow short-term burst to +1 node. Scale-down with 15m cooldown to avoid flapping.
- Fallbacks & cost control: route high-cost long generations to quantized variant; use TTL-based cache priming for top 10% sessions.

Action items: Ben, create a short doc (2–3 bullets) on SDK auth patterns (SAML + M2M rotation + Vault integration) and an example code snippet for prioritized routing. Rishi, I can draft the note back to Acme with the above and attach the modeling sheet.

Attachments to internal note: throughput-modeling-sheet.xlsx (updated)

Marissa

2) Autoscale: Floor = 2 nodes, warm-reserve = 1 pre-warmed node, scheduled scale-to-4 nodes 40m before reranker window, short burst allowed +1 node. Use a 15m cooldown on scale-down. This minimizes cold-starts while controlling idle cost.
